seoDescription: A Go author resurrects his seven-year-old minimal web framework WeaveBooks, reimplements example apps, compares routing, middleware, templating and group/box concepts, and runs micro-benchmarks against the popular GoFiber framework to measure latency and allocations. The video covers hands-on code restoration, compatibility fixes, middleware scoping, route parameters, and benchmark methodology and results for Go HTTP frameworks.

chapters.title: Intro: Rediscovering WeaveBooks and the Challenge
chapters.description: The author introduces WeaveBooks, its origin seven years ago, and sets up the goal to revive and benchmark it against GoFiber.

chapters.title: Cloning the Repo and Opening WeaveBooks
chapters.description: Clone the repository, open the project, and prepare an example folder to run WeaveBooks, including go.mod setup.

chapters.title: Building Routes and Parameters with WeaveBooks
chapters.description: Create GET routes, return text responses, test locally, and add route parameters for IDs.

chapters.title: Boxes, Grouping Routes and Middleware Scopes
chapters.description: Demonstrate boxed groups for modular routes, add separate boxes for users and books, and attach scoped middleware to boxes.

chapters.title: Preparing and Running Benchmarks Against GoFiber
chapters.description: Create benchmark tests for WeaveBooks, fix compatibility issues, add a Fiber benchmark, and compare allocations and ns/op.

chapters.title: Benchmark Results, Conclusions and Signoff
chapters.description: Share benchmark numbers showing WeaveBooks performance advantage, reflect on the findings, and provide final calls to action.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **WeaveBooks**: a minimal, backtrackable Go web framework written seven years ago that implements routing, boxed grouping, middleware scoping, static/template support, and a small API surface similar to modern frameworks.

- **Routing & Parameters**:
  - Define routes with app.Get and handler functions returning (error).
  - Access path parameters via **ctx.Param("id")** and respond with **ctx.Text(status, string)**.

- **Boxes / Groups**:
  - Use **app.Box("/prefix")** to create route groups (boxes) that namespace handlers.
  - Boxes allow modular organization of endpoints like `/users` and `/books`.

- **Middleware Scoping**:
  - Attach middleware per box using **box.Use(middleware)** to apply logic only to that group.
  - Middleware signature uses the framework **context** and returns an **error**.

- **Benchmarking Methodology**:
  - Create benchmark tests that simulate requests against the framework's Serve/Test method.
  - Compare allocations and ns/op between implementations (WeaveBooks vs GoFiber).

- **Results & Takeaways**:
  - The restored WeaveBooks showed very low allocations and sub-microsecond behavior in the demo benchmarks.
  - The author observed GoFiber to be slower in this specific test; benchmark numbers must be interpreted in their context and test setup.

> [!TIP] When restoring old code, fix small API/typing regressions (e.g., integer vs string fields) and update imports before running tests.

> [!NOTE] Benchmarks are sensitive to the exact handler implementations and test harness; always run benchmarks on the same machine and Go version for fair comparisons.

> [!IMPORTANT] Do not generalize a single benchmark to all workloads—measure with real application patterns relevant to your system.
